segments.name: AI-intensive software
segments.description: A controlled Flux evaluation in internal coding or knowledge work. Proprietary voice inference is a different purchase.

segments.name: Global workforce
segments.description: Country-specific documents, service requests, and operational handoffs. Keep payroll and employment decisions under existing authority.

segments.name: Financial operations
segments.description: The casework around money: investigation, onboarding, and follow-up. Existing ledgers and controls remain authoritative.

segments.name: Insurance operations
segments.description: Submission readiness and servicing across documents and portals. Licensed professionals retain coverage and binding decisions.

segments.name: ERP & implementation

segments.name: Controlled environments
segments.description: A later motion where infrastructure control matters enough to justify a longer evaluation and procurement cycle.

anchors.name: Deel
anchors.evidence: Eragon names Deel for Flux and Browser Use; its gateway reports a coding deployment across 2,000+ engineers.
anchors.logic: Two adjacencies: existing AI economics in engineering, and country-specific operational context. A shared industry does not establish an unmet need.

anchors.name: Slash
anchors.evidence: Eragon names Slash as a production customer for Flux and Browser Use. The announcements do not quantify savings.
anchors.logic: Follow financial-services casework that crosses support, records, and external systems. Do not pitch capabilities a prospect already sells.

anchors.name: Corgi
anchors.evidence: Eragon names Corgi in its Browser Use announcement. The proposed quote-preparation flows in this atlas are hypotheses.
anchors.logic: Explore the administrative work around insurance: complete submissions, retrieved documents, and follow-up. Underwriting and binding remain outside the initial scope.

anchors.name: Prodware
anchors.evidence: Eragon names Prodware for Flux and Browser Use. A customer relationship does not establish a reseller agreement.
anchors.logic: Test whether a repeated cross-system workflow earns a place beside an implementation partner’s existing Microsoft and AI capabilities.

prospects.name: ElevenLabs
prospects.evidence: Markets voice generation, developer APIs, and a conversational-agent platform.
prospects.adjacency: An AI-native developer business is adjacent to Deel’s reported coding-routing use, but its own agent platform raises build-versus-buy questions.
prospects.workflow: Evaluate Flux on an internal coding workload, with the existing route as the control.
prospects.constraint: Strong internal capability and an overlapping agent product. Do not assume its voice-serving stack is an Eragon routing opportunity.
prospects.expansion: Internal account research and implementation handoffs.
prospects.validate: Eligible internal spend, current routing, procurement owner, and performance on unseen tasks.
prospects.trigger: Unknown. Public positioning supports the adjacency; it does not establish an active buying project.
prospects.triggerHypothesis: A persistent queue, repeated document rework, or a service-level problem owned by the proposed buyer.

prospects.name: Deepgram
prospects.evidence: Describes a voice stack spanning speech recognition, LLM orchestration, and speech generation.
prospects.adjacency: Developer infrastructure suggests a possible internal engineering evaluation; published orchestration also makes replacement unlikely.
prospects.workflow: Route a bounded set of internal coding or research tasks across approved models.
prospects.constraint: Existing orchestration expertise and real-time requirements; separate internal work from customer-facing audio.
prospects.expansion: Approved internal knowledge workflows.
prospects.validate: A genuinely unserved workload and full cost including verification, latency, and retries.
prospects.trigger: Unknown. Public positioning supports the adjacency; it does not establish an active buying project.
prospects.triggerHypothesis: A measurable increase in eligible internal model cost, or an unresolved model-governance requirement.

prospects.name: AssemblyAI
prospects.evidence: Its official overview includes speech APIs, voice agents, and an LLM Gateway.
prospects.adjacency: Engineering context is adjacent, but a published gateway is a direct reason to question purchase intent.
prospects.workflow: Discovery only: determine whether internal knowledge or governance remains outside its gateway.
prospects.constraint: Substantial gateway and agent overlap. A generic model-routing pitch is weak.
prospects.expansion: Only a clearly differentiated internal workflow.
prospects.validate: Why its existing gateway cannot serve the proposed task.
prospects.trigger: Unknown. Public positioning supports the adjacency; it does not establish an active buying project.
prospects.triggerHypothesis: A measurable increase in eligible internal model cost, or an unresolved model-governance requirement.

bets.title: Start with casework.
bets.subtitle: Oyster · Relay
bets.body: I would look for a recurring service case that requires several systems and a human decision. Put the preparation and coordination under the agent; keep the decision with its owner.
bets.trigger: A measured backlog or missed service target; not yet verified.
bets.metric: Accepted cases per reviewer-hour, with no rise in reopens.
bets.risk: The existing support stack may already solve it.
bets.change: No repeated cross-system gap, or no owner willing to change the process.

bets.title: Make submissions ready.
bets.subtitle: Vouch · Coverdash
bets.body: I would test document completeness before quote preparation. It is narrow enough to audit and close enough to revenue to matter.
bets.trigger: A verified submission queue or repeat missing-document work.
bets.offer: One submission class, existing rating systems, broker approval.
bets.metric: Reviewer minutes and rework per accepted submission.
bets.risk: Native automation may cover most of the work.
bets.change: Low remaining handling time or unavailable carrier-portal permissions.

bets.title: Earn the routing layer.
bets.subtitle: Cartesia · ElevenLabs
bets.body: I would ask for a small sample of internal coding or knowledge tasks. Win on cost per accepted result before asking for a wider deployment.
bets.trigger: Eligible cost or governance friction; spend is unknown.
bets.offer: A controlled comparison against the current route.
bets.metric: All-in cost at an agreed quality and latency threshold.
bets.risk: These teams can build, and already sell agents.
bets.change: No cost-quality advantage after retries and verification.

deployments.label: Oyster
deployments.title: A service case, ready for its owner.
deployments.before: A proposed starting point: a country-specific request whose context is split across messages, documents, and case history. Current handling and tools must be established in discovery.
steps: Route to the case owner for review
deployments.systems: Case system, approved country knowledge, customer records, and communications. Exact systems are unknown.
deployments.approval: An authorized specialist approves employment guidance and any external response.
deployments.success: Lower reviewer time and shorter case turnaround, without worse corrections or reopen rates.
deployments.expand: Onboarding-document readiness → client handoffs → recurring service reviews.

deployments.label: Coverdash
deployments.title: A complete submission, before the quote.
deployments.before: Hypothesis: some submissions still require document chasing or inconsistent carrier packets. Confirm the uncovered case type before building.
steps: Check required fields against a checklist
Prepare a packet for broker approval
deployments.systems: Authorized intake records, document storage, approved carrier requirements, and permitted portal access.
deployments.approval: A licensed professional retains coverage, placement, and binding authority.
deployments.success: Less rework and fewer reviewer minutes per accepted submission; quote conversion is a later measure.
deployments.expand: Submission completeness → renewal packets → partner-service preparation.

deployments.label: Relay
deployments.title: An investigation with its evidence attached.
deployments.before: Hypothesis: a payment-service request needs evidence from more than one authorized source. Existing automation, volume, and permissions remain unknown.
steps: Hand off to the authorized reviewer
deployments.systems: Support cases, approved account metadata, transaction references, and internal procedures. No inferred production stack.
deployments.approval: The authorized team decides the response and any account action. The first agent does not move money.
deployments.success: Accepted packets per reviewer-hour, citation correctness, and unchanged or improved reopen rate.
deployments.expand: Investigation packets → approved follow-up preparation → internal service knowledge.
